threat_event: Attacker uses the shared OT remote access platform to reach several OT environments (DOP, transmission substations, Gas Production POC)
threat_source: Nation-state or criminal group targeting energy companies
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: One platform (SYS-G4) for three OT environments; 230 Engineering Services accounts with standing access to all three; per-session approval inconsistent; malicious-communication detection at only 31 of 74 substations
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 6.1-6.3); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: MFA at the gateway (SYS-G1); session recording; separate jump host clusters per environment
treatment_plan: Remove standing access; per-session approval by the OT owner; separate account sets per environment; malicious-communication detection on every vendor and engineer session

threat_event: Destructive or manipulative attack on the Distribution Operations Platform opens feeders, corrupts the OMS, and slows restoration
threat_source: Nation-state group pre-positioned in OT; criminal group pivoting from IT
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: DOP outside CIP scope with 37 broad IT/OT firewall rules; no OT monitoring in the DCC networks; backups on the same OT network; unsupported operator consoles
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-003-9 R2 Att. 1 Sec. 3.1 for traffic into low impact substations); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Manual switching procedures; backup DCC; storm drills; OT domain separate from SYS-G1
treatment_plan: Firewall rebuild with deny-by-default; OT sensors in the DCC networks; offline and immutable DOP backups with a full restore test; console replacement

threat_event: A cross-division incident is reported late or inconsistently to NERC, E-ISAC, CISA, DOE, clients, states, or the SEC
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Single notification matrix not exercised; DOE-417 cyber criteria missing from DCC procedures; Engineering Services has no register of client notice terms
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-008-6 R4); DOE-417; EOP-004-4 R2; SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
existing_controls: TCC reporting procedures; disclosure committee charter; group SOC
treatment_plan: Complete the matrix; cross-division tabletop including client notices and SEC materiality; DCC procedures with DOE-417 criteria

threat_event: AI models drive operational, purchasing, or client deliverables without validation, monitoring, or approved data use
threat_source: Model error; misuse of approved tools
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2025 load-forecasting model never independently validated; generative AI design assistant used with client documents before approval; Group AI Standard adopted after deployment
regulatory_driver: Group AI Standard (P10); client contracts (confidentiality)
existing_controls: Group AI council; approved-tools list
treatment_plan: Group AI program (P10): validation and drift monitoring for SYS-E6; client data rules for the design assistant

threat_event: Division controls fail silently because supplements have drifted and inheritance is undocumented
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Gas Production standards from 2023 conflict with 2026 group policy; inheritance documented for the Electric Utility only
affected_asset_or_process: Gas Production and Engineering Services control environments
regulatory_driver: Group policy POL-01 (4.5, 4.6)
existing_controls: Group policy office; annual policy cycle
treatment_plan: Re-issue the Gas Production supplement; inheritance matrices for Gas Production and Engineering Services; annual attestations

threat_event: Client CEII and BES Cyber System Information held by Engineering Services is exposed, including the Electric Utility's own BCSI
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Project platform permissions inherited by project-wide groups; client BCSI found in personal cloud storage; the Electric Utility's TCC BCSI stored on SYS-S1 outside its CIP-004 R6 access program
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-004-7 R6; CIP-011-3 R1); client contracts; 18 CFR 388.113
existing_controls: SOC 2 Type 1 controls on SYS-S1; encryption at rest; DLP on email
treatment_plan: Per-project access with client approval for CEII and BCSI folders; block personal cloud storage; bring Electric Utility BCSI on SYS-S1 into its CIP-004 R6 program
owner: Engineering Services security and compliance lead

threat_event: Compromised vendor software, firmware, or update channel reaches OT systems in several divisions
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: OT vendors shared across divisions (ADMS, EMS, relay, SCADA, remote access); software integrity checked for CIP systems but not for the DOP or field SCADA
existing_controls: CIP-013-2 plan for medium impact systems; hash verification for EMS patches
treatment_plan: Extend the CIP-013 integrity and vendor notice processes to the DOP and field SCADA; group OT vendor tiering

threat_event: Ransomware spreads through shared IT services and halts Engineering Services, corporate, and division business systems
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Shared identity, WAN, and cloud platform; flat office networks at older Engineering Services offices
regulatory_driver: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05; client contracts
existing_controls: 24x7 SOC; EDR; PAM; immutable cloud backups
treatment_plan: Office network segmentation; quarterly restore tests of SYS-S1; tabletop with the disclosure committee

threat_event: Potential CIP noncompliance leads to penalties, mitigation burden, and closer SERC oversight
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Six potential noncompliances found in 2026 (P03); new CIP-003-9 and CIP-012-2 obligations took effect in 2026
existing_controls: NERC compliance program; internal controls testing
treatment_plan: Self-report by 2026-09-30 with mitigation plans; quarterly CIP internal controls review

threat_event: A privileged insider misuses OT access to disrupt operations
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Broad OT domain administrator rights (14 accounts in the DOP); shared field SCADA accounts at Gas Production
regulatory_driver: N22-R01 (CIP-004-7 R3 for TCC); Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Personnel risk assessments for OT administrators; session recording
treatment_plan: Reduce DOP domain administrators; named accounts at Gas Production; behavior analytics on OT logs

threat_event: Physical attack on a transmission substation or control center disrupts operations
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 74 transmission substations, some in remote areas; firearms damage to transformers is a known industry threat
regulatory_driver: EOP-004-4 R2; DOE-417 criteria 1 and 10
existing_controls: Fencing, cameras, and alarms; hardened control centers
treatment_plan: Risk-ranked hardening for 12 substations; response drills with law enforcement
owner: Electric Utility security and compliance lead

threat_event: A critical SaaS or cloud vendor (AMI, CIS, cloud provider) suffers an outage or breach
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: AMI head-end and CIS are vendor SaaS; AMI SOC 2 report has exceptions (P09)
regulatory_driver: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6) (third-party agent notice); client contracts
existing_controls: Vendor SOC 2 reviews; contract notice terms for new contracts
treatment_plan: Annual SOC 2 reviews with exception follow-up; AMI command limits; exit plans

threat_event: Personal information of customers, royalty owners, or workforce is stolen
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 2.4 million customer records in the CIS (SSNs for some); 48,000 royalty owners with SSNs; HR data for 45,000 employees
regulatory_driver: State breach laws (Fla. Stat. 501.171 worked example); SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
existing_controls: Encryption; MFA; vendor SOC 2 reviews
treatment_plan: Data minimization (stop storing SSNs after credit checks); royalty data access review

threat_event: A major hurricane damages control centers and disrupts IT at the same time as grid restoration
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Florida service area; corporate HQ and the DCC in the same county
regulatory_driver: EOP-004-4; DOE-417 criterion 12
existing_controls: Backup TCC and DCC in another county; storm plans exercised each May
treatment_plan: Move the backup DCC warm standby to hot standby; satellite communications at the backup DCC

threat_event: The group misjudges or delays a materiality decision after a cybersecurity incident
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Disclosure committee has not exercised an OT incident with grid impact and client notices
regulatory_driver: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05; Reg S-K Item 106
existing_controls: Disclosure committee cybersecurity charter
treatment_plan: Include the disclosure committee in the cross-division tabletop (P08)

threat_event: A cyber event at Gas Production cuts fuel to generators that supply the Electric Utility during peak demand
threat_source: Attacker or failure affecting field SCADA
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Two plants fueled by Gas Production supply about 30% of the Electric Utility purchased power; Gas field SCADA has weak access controls
regulatory_driver: Firm supply contracts; N21-BM (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Generators hold limited backup fuel; Electric Utility can buy replacement power
treatment_plan: Joint peak-season plans; Gas Production SCADA hardening (GP-001)

threat_event: Business email compromise diverts payments in any division
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: High volume of vendor and royalty payments; supplier bank changes by email
regulatory_driver: SEC internal control over financial reporting
existing_controls: MFA; payment change callbacks in finance
treatment_plan: Extend callback controls to Gas Production royalty changes and Engineering Services subcontractor payments

threat_event: Engineering Services fails a federal contract safeguarding requirement
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: FCI on SYS-S1 under the same controls as client data; no FAR clause register
existing_controls: SOC 2 controls on SYS-S1
treatment_plan: FAR clause register; annual 52.204-21 self-check

threat_event: Cloud misconfiguration exposes data on the group platform
threat_source: Configuration error exploited by an attacker
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: Guardrails cover provider A fully but provider B accounts for SYS-S1 only partly
regulatory_driver: Client contracts; SOC 2 commitments
existing_controls: Guardrail policies; posture management in provider A
treatment_plan: Extend guardrails and posture management to all provider B accounts

threat_event: Unsupported OT components across divisions cannot be patched when a vulnerability is exploited
vulnerability_or_predisposing_condition: 22 DOP operator consoles and 40 gas RTUs past vendor support
regulatory_driver: Voluntary benchmark (NIST CSF 2.0; SP 800-82 Rev. 3)
existing_controls: Network isolation; application allowlisting on servers
treatment_plan: Replace consoles in 2027; RTU replacement in the 2027 capital plan
